# Decisions: record-integrity

- 2026-08-01T17:31:20.624Z — chose **Derive a session's home initiative from the event logs themselves — scan for the session's earliest session_started, checking the branch-bound initiative first and only falling through to siblings on a miss** over A new .sofar/sessions.json index mapping session_id to slug, written at registration and read by hooks because The home is ALREADY in the truth log — session_started names it uniquely — so an index file would be duplicated state that can desync, needs pruning (99 sessions and counting), and forces a SPEC Record-layout change plus a gitignore decision (routing is a local runtime fact, but .sofar/ is committed wholesale). Deriving costs one file read on the common path (branch is correct → hit on the first log checked) and only pays the sibling scan in exactly the case where a misroute would otherwise have happened; total log volume is ~350KB. It is also self-healing: sessions registered before this fix get pinned correctly with no migration. Same philosophy as reading git state rather than logging it — a fact with an authoritative home is read, never copied.
- 2026-08-01T17:41:22.869Z — chose **Pin start_session to the session home as well as the hooks — branch resolution now applies only when `initiative` is explicit or the session has no home** over Pinning hooks alone (the original Phase 1 scope), or using envelope.source to tell a deliberate re-home from a misroute because Measuring the 14 double-registrations in this repo inverted the hypothesis: 11 are hook-then-claude-code across two initiatives, i.e. the tear is NOT mostly a mid-session branch switch but lazy registration racing start_session — the hook registers in the branch's initiative, the binding moves, and start_session registers the SAME id again elsewhere. Hook pinning alone would have left those 11 intact. The source-based heuristic was rejected by the same data: the second registration is usually claude-code, so treating claude-code as deliberate would suppress 11 of 14 real splits.
